errors.location: Materials and methods — AUC trapezoidal formula
errors.description: The stated trapezoidal AUC formula omits the factor of 1/2. As written, each interval contributes twice the standard trapezoid area, so AUC values calculated with this formula would be doubled.
errors.evidence: The manuscript gives AUC = Σ(Cᵢ + Cᵢ₊₁)·(tᵢ₊₁ − tᵢ), without dividing by 2.

errors.location: Results — Pharmacokinetic result; absorption rate constant
errors.description: The reported absorption rate range is inconsistent with the stated equation and the muscle absorption half-life: 17.23 h implies Kₐ ≈ 0.040 h⁻¹, outside the reported range.
errors.evidence: The manuscript states Kₐ = ln(2)/t₁/₂a, gives muscle t₁/₂a as 17.23 h, and reports Kₐ values of 0.0002–0.011 h⁻¹.

errors.location: Results — Pharmacokinetic result; elimination half-lives; Conclusion
errors.description: The reported elimination half-lives conflict, and the conclusion identifies the liver as having the longest half-life despite the Results giving a much longer plasma value.
errors.evidence: The Results give liver t₁/₂b as 238.68 h and later as 420.28 h; they also report plasma at 3368.24 h. The Conclusion calls the liver half-life of 238.68 h the longest.

errors.description: The reported R² values do not support the claimed calibration linearity: R² cannot exceed 1, and a value of 0.002 indicates essentially no fit.
errors.evidence: The manuscript reports an R² of 6.96 for muscle and 0.002 for skin, while describing R² as reflecting calibration linearity.

errors.description: Negative LOD and LOQ values are not physically meaningful concentration limits, so interpreting them as evidence of minimal detectable drug presence is invalid.
errors.evidence: The manuscript reports kidney LOD −587.51 µg kg⁻¹ and LOQ −1780.34 µg kg⁻¹, then states that negative LOD/LOQ values suggest minimal drug presence.

errors.location: Discussion — muscle residue and consumer safety
errors.description: The claim that residues in the 1× and 3× groups remained below the EU MRL conflicts with the reported day-20 maxima, both of which exceed the stated 100 µg kg⁻¹ MRL.
errors.evidence: The manuscript reports day-20 muscle concentrations of 118 µg kg⁻¹ at 1× and 351 µg kg⁻¹ at 3×, then says residues remained below the 100 µg kg⁻¹ MRL in those groups.

errors.description: The baseline creatinine results conflict after unit conversion: 0.2 mg/L equals 0.02 mg/dL, not the 0.05 mg/dL stated for the control group.
errors.evidence: The table gives control creatinine as 0.2 mg/L on day 0; the accompanying text gives the control level as 0.05 ± 0.001 mg/dL.

errors.location: Materials and methods — biosafety dosing; Results — feeding behavior
errors.description: The manuscript reports only 80–90% consumption of medicated feed, while describing the groups by the nominal feed dose. Unless the dose was adjusted for uneaten feed, the fish's actual exposure was below the stated dose, leaving the claimed dose-specific safety assessment uncertain.
errors.evidence: The methods specify doses of 80, 240, 400, and 800 mg kg⁻¹ fish day⁻¹; the Results state that only 80–90% of feed was consumed during medicated feeding.
